title: POST /api/v1/positions performs presence-only validation: null values and untyped fields reach PositionService and surface as 500s
reasoning: The required-field check uses `body.tickLower === undefined`, so explicit nulls (JSON null) pass validation, and tickLower/tickUpper are never type/range-checked (floats, strings, and booleans all pass), liquidity/amount0/amount1 are never format-checked, protocol is not constrained to 'v3'|'v4', and tokenId is not validated. Malformed input therefore fails inside PositionService and is reported as a generic 500 with String(err) instead of a 400. This is inconsistent with the strictly validated reconcile endpoints in the same file (lines 120, 158) and the tp-sl create handler. Confidence is low because the service layer is not among the included files, but the pass-through of unvalidated null values is visible in the route itself.
reproduction: POST /api/v1/positions with a valid session and body {poolId:'0x…', tickLower:null, tickUpper:100, liquidity:'1000'} — the null passes the === undefined check and the request fails downstream with 500.
recommendation: Add explicit type/format/range validation for tickLower, tickUpper (integers), liquidity, amount0, amount1 (uint strings), protocol (enum), and tokenId, returning 400 on violations.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No positions route tests are included in the feature's test set.
suggestedRegressionTest: POST /positions with tickLower:null (and with non-integer liquidity) must return 400 before touching the service.
